4	/* HTIF syscall-window client: the uncached SimControl mailbox protocol
5	 * shared by every andesim runtime payload (vplat today; vlinux next). The
6	 * window lives in DEVICE space (PMA-uncached on every engine), so the
7	 * exchange is coherent by construction on any cache hierarchy, including a
8	 * private write-back L2 (ax66 PL2C) that a cacheable-RAM mailbox cannot
9	 * survive: the guest would read its own stale copy of the host's result,
10	 * and no guest-side CCTL sequence can fix that (the VA-scoped forms trap
11	 * on RVH cores, the ALL forms drop unrelated dirty lines).
12	 *
13	 *   stdio (fd 0-2)  ATCUART100 UART2: THR @0xf0300020, LSR @0xf0300034.
14	 *   file io (fd>2)  the SimControl syscall WINDOW @0xe0080800: eight u64
15	 *                   arg/result slots + a data area for payloads, doorbell
16	 *                   @0xe0080028. Served host-side (vsim: sim_control.hpp
17	 *                   dispatch_window; QEMU: andes_ae350.c's mirror).
18	 *

2	 *
3	 * Load base: 0x00100000 (1 MiB into andes_ae350 DRAM).
4	 *
5	 * andes_ae350 memory map:
6	 *   DRAM : 0x00000000 .. 0x7FFFFFFF  (writable, executable)
7	 *   MROM : 0x80000000 .. 0x87FFFFFF  (read-only)
8	 *
9	 * Reserved scratch (below text, used by .S fixtures):
10	 *   0x00000004              rt_csr_survival mtvec test value
11	 *   0x00001000              semihost_exit.inc param block
12	 *   0x00002000              rt_all_gprs spill area
13	 *   0x00003000              rt_mem_loadstore / rt_unaligned_lh buffer
14	 *   0x00010000              rt_shared_mem 4 KB buffer
15	 *
16	 * Layout above 0x00100000:
17	 *   .text         pinned at 0x00100000 (entry _start)
18	 *   .rodata
19	 *   .preinit_array/.init_array/.fini_array + EH tables (C++ runtime;
20	 *                 deliberately ABOVE _edata, see the comment there)
21	 *   .data         _edata terminates .data
22	 *   .bss          _end   terminates .bss (crt0 zeros [.bss, _end))
23	 *   _stack        0x00700000 (used by crt0.S to init sp)
24	 *
25	 * V-register transport scratch (L26): NOT a fixed address any more. The driver
26	 * maps one 4 KiB page above --mem-size and parks the scratch there (the mmap's
27	 * top page, v_scratch_gpa = ram_base + --mem-size), so it sits just past the
28	 * program's RAM -- nothing in this script can collide with it. No reservation
29	 * needed here.
30	 *
31	 * .S fixtures with no .data/.bss leave those sections empty (zero cost).
32	 * C fixtures rely on _edata / _end / _stack.
33	 */

36	
37	SECTIONS {
38	    . = 0x00100000;
39	
40	    .text : {
41	        *(.text.init)
42	        *(.text*)
43	    }
44	
45	    .rodata : {
46	        *(.rodata*)
47	        *(.srodata*)
48	    }

50	    /* C++ constructor/destructor arrays and EH metadata. Everything here
51	     * must stay ABOVE _edata: crt0 zeroes [_edata, _end) before it walks
52	     * .init_array, so an array placed after .data would be wiped first.
53	     * crt0.S runs newlib's __libc_init_array, which reads the WEAK
54	     * start/end symbols below -- without these PROVIDEs they resolve to
55	     * 0 and no constructor ever runs. KEEP: entries are only referenced
56	     * through these bounds, never by symbol. */
57	    .preinit_array : {
58	        PROVIDE_HIDDEN(__preinit_array_start = .);
59	        KEEP(*(.preinit_array))
60	        PROVIDE_HIDDEN(__preinit_array_end = .);
61	    }
62	    .init_array : {
63	        PROVIDE_HIDDEN(__init_array_start = .);
64	        KEEP(*(SORT_BY_INIT_PRIORITY(.init_array.*) SORT_BY_INIT_PRIORITY(.ctors.*)))
65	        KEEP(*(.init_array .ctors))
66	        PROVIDE_HIDDEN(__init_array_end = .);
67	    }
68	    .fini_array : {
69	        PROVIDE_HIDDEN(__fini_array_start = .);
70	        KEEP(*(SORT_BY_INIT_PRIORITY(.fini_array.*) SORT_BY_INIT_PRIORITY(.dtors.*)))

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Runtime-lib F2 contract: `make -C runtime` produces a linkable library
# under build/runtime/ so users stop listing the 4 runtime sources:
#
#   build/runtime/libandesim_runtime.a   (trap.o handler.o htif_client.o vplat_syscalls.o)
#   build/runtime/crt0.o                   (startfile; OUTSIDE the archive)
#   build/runtime/andesim.ld             (linker script)
#
# Probe: link vplat_hello.c with the raw library line (no specs file yet)
# and run it on the cycle engine -- prints via UART, exits 0 via SimControl.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:?config.env missing}"
GCC="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc"
NM="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm"

SIM="$(vsim_bin_dir)/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
[ -x "$SIM" ] || fail "cycle engine not found (source ./setup.sh): $SIM"

make -C "$ROOT/runtime" || fail "runtime lib build failed"

RT="$ROOT/build/runtime"
[ -f "$RT/libandesim_runtime.a" ] || fail "missing $RT/libandesim_runtime.a"
[ -f "$RT/crt0.o" ] || fail "missing $RT/crt0.o"
[ -f "$RT/andesim.ld" ] || fail "missing $RT/andesim.ld"

# crt0 must be a standalone startfile: the archive never gets _start pulled.
# (grep without -q: early-exit + pipefail turns a MATCH into SIGPIPE failure)
"$NM" "$RT/crt0.o" | grep ' T _start' >/dev/null \
  || fail "crt0.o does not define _start"
"$NM" "$RT/libandesim_runtime.a" | grep ' T _write' >/dev/null \
  || fail "archive does not define _write"
"$NM" "$RT/libandesim_runtime.a" | grep ' T m_trap_entry' >/dev/null \
  || fail "archive does not define m_trap_entry"

# Raw (non-specs) link: what a non-gcc-driver build system would write.
TMP=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
"$GCC" -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -static -nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs \
  -T "$RT/andesim.ld" "$RT/crt0.o" "$ROOT/tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.c" \
  -L "$RT" -Wl,--start-group -landesim_runtime -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group \
  -o "$TMP/hello.elf" || fail "raw -landesim_runtime link failed"

OUT=$(timeout 120 "$SIM" "$TMP/hello.elf" </dev/null 2>&1); RC=$?
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'hello from vplat' \
  || fail "cycle: missing 'hello from vplat' in: $OUT"
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "cycle: exit code $RC != 0 (output: $OUT)"

ok "F2 libandesim_runtime.a links and runs on the cycle engine"

findings.title: crt0.S writes uninitialized a0 into mcache_ctl when ENABLE_DCACHE_COHERENCE is undefined (always)
findings.detail: The only instruction that loads a0 before line 35 is `csrr a0, mcache_ctl` at line 24, which is inside `#ifdef ENABLE_DCACHE_COHERENCE` (lines 19-32). Grep over the whole repo shows ENABLE_DCACHE_COHERENCE is never defined anywhere (only the #ifdef in crt0.S itself; runtime/Makefile CFLAGS is `$(ARCHFLAGS) -O1 -Wall` with no -D, and tests/fixtures/Makefile only builds crt0 via `$(MAKE) -C runtime`, lines 217/241). So in every shipped build, line 35 `ori a0, a0, 0x703` ORs the boot-entry value of a0 and line 36 `csrw mcache_ctl, a0` writes it wholesale (csrw, not csrs), clobbering the icache-enable done at line 17. It works today only because hart 0 enters _start with a0=0 on both engines (all e2e tests pass), i.e. correct by accident. Proper fix: `csrr a0, mcache_ctl` before the ori (which also preserves the line-17 bit instead of relying on 0x703 containing bit 0). On current engines that writes the identical value 0x703, so the fix is observably behavior-preserving, but since it changes what a latent-buggy instruction computes it should be handled in the bug track, not the structural-refactor track.
findings.safety: Not a structural change - flagged for separate handling per instructions. The minimal fix (csrr before ori) provably writes the same 0x703 on both current engines given mcache_ctl reset=0 plus the line-17 csrsi.

findings.title: LOAD x0 in the trap-exit register restore is an architectural no-op
findings.detail: Line 101 `LOAD x0, 0*REGBYTES(sp)` loads the frame slot back into x0; RISC-V discards writes to x0, so the instruction has no architectural effect (the memory read is from the just-written stack frame, same page as the adjacent restores, so no fault-behavior difference either). The matching STORE x0 at line 24 IS load-bearing - it defines regs[0]=0 in the frame contract documented by ecall_hook.h ('regs[N] is xN for N in {0,1,3..31}') - so only the LOAD should go. This file is vendor-derived (Andes copyright header, 'NOT ... for production'), so the team may prefer keeping it verbatim; if so, skip.
findings.safety: rd=x0 makes the instruction a no-op by ISA definition; removing it changes no register, no memory, no trap behavior - only one fewer instruction on the trap-return path (not inside any measured ROI contract).

findings.title: Never-active extern "C" wrapper and no-effect used-attribute on a declaration in handler.c
findings.detail: handler.c wraps its whole body in `#ifdef __cplusplus extern "C" {` (lines 12-15, closed 117-119), but the file is only ever compiled as C: the sole compile rule is runtime/Makefile's gcc `.c` rule (line 65); tests/fixtures/Makefile lists handler.c only as a prerequisite (RUNTIME_DEPS, lines 61-67) and builds via `$(MAKE) -C runtime` (line 217), and the C++ fixture (vplat_cpp) links the prebuilt archive, not sources. So __cplusplus is never defined here and the guard is dead. Relatedly, line 28's `__attribute__((used, noreturn))` sits on a mere DECLARATION of _exit - `used` has no effect on declarations (the definition in vplat_syscalls.c line 195 carries its own attributes); only the noreturn is meaningful there.
findings.safety: Removing a preprocessor branch that never activates and an attribute that has no effect on a declaration cannot change the emitted object; handler.o is bit-identical after the change.

findings.title: _getcwd declares its output buffer const and casts the const away internally
findings.detail: `int _getcwd(const char* buf, int size)` (line 152) is an output-parameter function: line 159 does `htif_win_load((void*) buf, 0, n)`, writing the host's cwd string through the pointer after casting away the const. The const qualifier misstates the contract (getcwd fills the buffer) and forces the cast. Changing the parameter to `char* buf` removes the lie and the cast. The sibling implementation runtime/linux/syscall.c sys_getcwd (line 396) already uses the non-const `char* buf` signature for the same operation.
findings.safety: Top-level pointer qualifiers do not affect the calling convention or mangling in C; the symbol, ABI, and generated code are unchanged (the cast merely disappears at the source level).
